content: Discussion thread for the next 6 months roadmap of the Mathlib Initiative

The roadmap says "Second, we widen the pool of people able to review, through supporting training events." Can we hear more details about this? I learned some useful tricks from reading others review comments on any random PR that caught me. I suppose such training events would be more efficient than browsing the PR queue.
There'll be an announcement of the next such event hopefully today!

I support increasing review capacity and growing Mathlib faster. But one concern I have is that a wider pool of reviewers and higher AI use in reviews will lead to PRs pulling designs in different directions, or, worse, duplicating mathematical concepts altogether.

Of course, this already happened in the past - for instance, there's about 5 different ways to adjoin a root of a polynomial to a field. But it happened slowly enough that Zulip design discussions could generally cover the issues and lead to refacactors that were viable to merge.

I worry that the relatively small segment of the Mathlib community actively thinking about high-level design will be overwhelmed once the library grows more quickly.

Has MI considered how to address this?

Has there been any discussion about coordination between the FRO's downstream-lean4 and MI's downstream-reports? At the moment it's a bit of a niche question, because CSLib is the only repo that participates in both. Maybe it's a non-issue if this intersection remains small, but maybe this grows? I could imagine more projects with a Mathlib dependency also wanting nightly toolchain testing.
There has indeed been some coordination. :thumbs_up:

Michael Rothgang said:

There'll be an announcement of the next such event hopefully today!

Here it is: #Event announcements > Mathlib reviewer bootcamp 2027 Applications are welcome!

Johan Commelin said:

There has indeed been some coordination. :thumbs_up:

Good to hear! If later it's helpful, I'd be happy to share any feedback. (I don't have a strong opinion yet since CSLib just switched over fully to downstream-lean4 this week.)
